note: Modeled deterministic consumption-contract vectors, in the ROS2 request/expect form. candidateEnvelope supplies an already evaluated envelope fixture, not an A/E computation formula. Except for the signed cryptographic fixtures, trustedFixtures represent supplied verification/status outcomes and do not claim cryptographic verification or real measurement. Unless stage is observation_freshness, every vector begins with all other required contracts satisfied. observation_freshness cases exercise only the freshness predicate and make no full-action or authorization assertion. decision is a derived vector reading, never a new wire result enum. tighter outcomes are permitted for monotonic pairs; S33 withholds the oversized request; S34 preserves the supervision floor and ceilings. Runtime implementations and real signature/current-state acquisition are external; vector/schema checks are prerequisites, never runtime certification. The trustedFixtures flags are supplied assumptions, and passing those cases does not establish the runtime contract. conditions supplies the governing observed values of repairPathVerified and supervisionAvailable.
timeNotation: Vector times and ages are integer milliseconds aligned to whole Unix seconds, the declared fixture resolution; decision wire timestamps are Unix seconds. Freshness equality is stale. S22/S51/S52 test the observation-freshness predicate independently, with no consumption decision. S39 tests decision expiry while the observation is fresh. Diagnostic expected fields are not new decision wire members.

schemaFixtureNote: Synthetic shape-only fixture. Digest strings and JWS segments are placeholders, not verified digests, a valid signature or an ordinary proof. It must never be used as authority. schemaVectors apply each isolated mutation to a fresh copy; omitted mutation means unchanged. Schema acceptance does not imply temporal, binding, token-representation or cryptographic acceptance.

rationale: Modeled shape fixture; not signed authority.

cryptographicFixtureNote: These cases exercise a signature-and-binding stage using ES256 and the published fixture-only public key. ordinaryProof is an opaque, complete signed test artifact, not a schema-valid KTP Trust Proof. ordinaryAuthorization and other required prerequisite/status checks remain explicitly supplied assumptions. cryptographicChecks are independent normative diagnostic outcomes, not new wire members; neither a generic deny nor those assumptions substitute for the required signature and binding checks. S53 is the positive stage control. The fixture key has no authority and no private key is published.
